questions.q:
Mention the types of polymers formed on the basis of intermolecular forces.



Write any two uses of low density polyethylene.
questions.solution:
1. Elastomers: Weak intermolecular forces, high elasticity (e.g., Natural rubber, Neoprene).
  2. Fibres: Strong hydrogen bonding, high tensile strength (e.g., Nylon, Terylene).
  3. Thermoplastic polymers: Intermediate forces, can be reshaped on heating (e.g., PVC, Polyethylene).
  4. Thermosetting polymers: Strong cross-linking, rigid structure (e.g., Bakelite, Melamine).


  1. Low density polyethylene (LDP) is mainly used in the preparation of pipes for agriculture, irrigation, domestic water line connections, as well as insulation to electric cables. It is also used in submarine cable insulation.
  2. It is used in producing extruded films, sheets, mainly for packaging and household uses like in preparation of squeeze bottles, attractive containers, etc.

questions.q:
Explain the given terms: Homopolymers



Explain the given terms : Elastomers
questions.solution:
Homopolymers: Polymers whose repeating structural units are derived from only one type of monomer units are called homopolymers.
Ex : – Polythene (prepared by using only one type of monomer i.e. ethene)



Elastomers: The polymers that have the elastic character like rubber are called elastomers.
Elastomers are soft & stretchy used to make rubber bands.
Ex: Neoprene, Vulcanized rubber etc.

questions.q: Write classification of polymers on the basis of structure.
questions.solution:
On the basis of structure polymers are classified in three types:

  1. Linear or straight-chain polymers: When monomer molecules are joined together in a linear arrangement, a straight-chain polymer is created. For example: High-density polymer (Polythene), PVC (Polyvinyl chloride).
  2. Branched-chain polymers: Branching-chain polymers are created when a monomer has three functional groups or already has side chains. As an example, consider low-density polythene.
  3. Cross linked polymers: This type of polymer is created by cross-linking linear chains to form a network-like structure. Bakelite, melamine, and other similar materials are examples.
